implementation.mathematics: For an affine map f(x)=ax+b, |a|<1, the unique fixed point is b/(1-a), and s_n-z=a^n(y-z). Therefore |s_n-z|=|a|^n|y-z| and |s_n-s_m| is at most the sum of the two errors. All values are mathematical data in Substance; both complete R, its Euclidean metric and the fixed point are explicit.
implementation.reuse: One parameterized Substance factory and one Style render both monotone and alternating sequences. A zero-slope constant map is verified as a third independent native-render case.

verification.native: All three programs converge through native Penrose optimization, with XML-valid SVG and annotation dragging.
verification.visual: Both white-background full-resolution native previews inspected; alternating fixed-point and initial labels moved clear of the cobweb.

limits: These diagrams illustrate the complete real-line case of the exercise; they do not reconstruct a source figure or assert fixed-point existence in incomplete spaces.
The eight rendered steps do not enumerate the infinite sequence. The algebraic all-n identity establishes the error behavior, with ordinary floating-point evaluation in the helper.
The error chart rescales its vertical range by the initial error, so it shows relative geometric decay rather than a shared absolute vertical scale with the cobweb.
